conclusion: A specific statutory-clarity concern survives. Current Hpt186(9a) selects non-leverage risks where the corrected EU sentence selects excessive-leverage risks. The precise EU capital-quality result is already MNB’s published supervisory position, and binding individual requirements can be imposed under186(10). Neither the non-binding manual nor an unexamined possibility of individual decisions establishes a generally binding cure of the reversed statutory trigger. No capital shortage, deficient bank or incorrect supervisory decision is established.

reasoningLimits: Do not describe the manual as absent, generic or requiring only an undefined level of leverage oversight: it states minimumTier1 precisely.
Do not infer that MNB cannot impose or has not imposed a fully compliant binding requirement in any individual decision.
Do not infer that the statutory non-leverageTier1 rule is itself unlawful: higher supervisory capital-quality requirements may be permitted.
The unresolved point is whether a clear generally binding rule supplies the corrected leverage trigger despite186(9a),not whether every national provision reproduces the EU words.
The manual has appropriate public visibility; the concern relies on its expressly non-binding character and the contrary statutory selector,not on secrecy.

proposedPatch.statusLabel: Statutory wording differs · supervisory practice follows EU rule
proposedPatch.summary: Hungary’s statute retains the reversed risk selector corrected in the EU text. MNB’s current manual nevertheless directs at leastTier1 capital for leverage-ratio requirements. The remaining concern is statutory clarity; individual supervisory requirements can supply the required result.
proposedPatch.nationalGap: Hpt186(9a) expressly selects risks other than excessive leverage. MNB’s published2026 supervisory manual states the correct minimumTier1 treatment for leverage-ratio requirements, and186(10) permits a binding higher-quality requirement for an individual institution. MNB describes methodological manuals as non-binding supervisory instruments. Whether another generally binding measure cures the statutory selector remains unresolved.
proposedPatch.consequence: The statutory wording and the EU correction differ. Published MNB supervision follows the correctedTier1 composition, so no capital shortfall or incorrect bank requirement is established. A limited legal-certainty question remains about the general statutory rule.
